title: Weight-only INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ) integration and regression validation pipeline
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Add first-class support and automated regression testing for weight-only INT8 quantization using GPTQ and AWQ toolchains. This ticket covers integration into the model build pipeline, calibration artifact standardization, CI/nightly regression jobs, and an accuracy validation harness that produces deterministic pass/fail signals for alerts and rollouts.
background: We currently ship FP16 and FP8 recommendations for many models, but weight-only INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ) is increasingly valuable for cost-sensitive production workloads. Prior experiments show model-dependent accuracy trade-offs; without automated validation and calibrated baselines we risk regressions in customer-facing deployments. This work standardizes profiles, adds calibration artifacts to model packages, and creates regression gates in CI to surface quality drift.
approach: 1) Define canonical quantization profile manifest fields for weight-only INT8 (per-layer clipping, group size, scale type, activation fallback hints). 2) Implement adapters in the model packaging tool to attach GPTQ/AWQ artifacts and a calibration summary (calibration dataset fingerprint, max/min statistics, per-layer scale histograms). 3) Add a validation harness that runs a lightweight set of generation and discriminative evals (LAMBADA word prediction, WikiText-103 perplexity subset, cosine similarity on reference embeddings) and computes regression deltas against the signed golden baseline. 4) Wire nightly CI jobs that run on representative model families and create alerting tickets on >0.5% relative degradation on primary metrics or regressions on critical prompts. 5) Provide a manual QA dashboard and developer CLI to re-run calibration and gated tests locally.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical INT8 profile schema published and documented in docs/quantization-profiles.md
Model packaging attaches GPTQ/AWQ artifacts and a calibration-summary.json with deterministic keys
Validation harness produces numeric metrics and a pass/fail verdict for every model+profile combination
Nightly CI runs produce trend charts and create a Linear incident when a baseline regression threshold is crossed
Engineers can reproduce calibration+validation locally with a single CLI command and a stable seed
test_plan: Unit tests for profile serialization and manifest parsing, integration tests that run the quantize->pack->validate flow on three reference models (opt-1.3b, redwood-alpaca-7b, and a gpt-like 125M), include seeded RNGs for deterministic outputs. Nightly matrix of models x profiles with failure triage metadata. Performance smoke tests to ensure quantized artifacts are loadable in serving runtime with <5% median latency regression on synthetic traffic.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal integration branch with model packaging and local validation support. Phase 2: enable nightly regression jobs and alerting for core model families. Phase 3: enable automated gating for canary rollouts where if a profile fails validation it cannot be auto-promoted. Provide rollback instructions and an emergency disable feature for the CI gate.
notes: Calibration artifacts should be compact (prefer JSON + compressed histogram blobs) and signed. We should avoid shipping raw calibration datasets; instead include dataset fingerprints and sampling parameters. Coordinate with runtime team on loader API changes: add support for weight-only scale maps. Consider adding 'safety fallback' policy to use FP16 variant automatically when critical prompts degrade beyond threshold.
